placement.position_note: PLACED 2026-08-11. THE CORNER IS DOCUMENTED AND THE COORDINATE IS DERIVED, so the tag follows the weaker half. Andreas puts the log jail on 'the northwest corner of the court-house square'. The public square is the block bounded by Randolph Street on the north, Washington Street on the south, Clark Street on the east and LaSalle Street on the west - the block this project's own ground control identifies as such in data/traces/gcp/wright_1834_gcps.json, where LaSalle and Randolph is labelled 'NW corner of the Public Square block' and Clark and Washington 'SE corner of the Public Square block'. Its four inside corners were computed for this parcel from modern OpenStreetMap intersection centres fetched 2026-08-11, offset 12.2 m into the block on each axis, half of an 80 ft street per Hathaway 1834: NW 447538.25 / 4637130.78, NE 447639.27 / 4637130.25, SW 447541.20 / 4637018.49, SE 447639.80 / 4637018.05, which makes the block about 101 x 112 m. The jail's own north-west corner is set on the square's north-west corner, so the footprint origin - which is the building's south-west corner - sits its own depth south of it. THIS IS A CORNER OF A BLOCK, NOT A LOT, so it is a weaker statement than the corner-lot placements elsewhere in this dataset: nothing says how far into the block the building stood, whether it was set back from either street line, or which way it faced. WORKING UNCERTAINTY ABOUT 20 M from the georeference (data/datum.json: 17.5 m RMS on Wright 1834, 3.7 per cent paper stretch), plus an unquantified setback into the block. Facade bearing 0, due north onto Randolph, CONVENTION RATHER THAN EVIDENCE - a jail at the north-west corner could as reasonably have faced west onto LaSalle or inward onto the square, and nothing attests it. The square itself in 1835 was otherwise an open, unimproved prairie block, fenced or not; no fence, path or improvement of the block is modelled. RECONCILED WITH THE COMMITTED PLAT 2026-08-28 (T-0246), AND THE CLAIM DID NOT MOVE - ONLY THE LINE IT WAS DERIVED AGAINST. The method above found the square's north-west corner by taking modern OpenStreetMap intersection centres, fetched 2026-08-11, and stepping 12.2 m into the block on each axis. That is not this project's own Randolph Street: the committed centreline in data/streets/1835.json, offset by half the committed 80 ft corridor, is what tools/generate_plat_lots.py builds every platted block edge from, and it is the line every derived layer in this scene reads. Measured against it with tools/measure_corridor_intrusion.py, this footprint's north wall stood 3.48 m OUT PAST blk_randolph_lasalle's Randolph frontage line, in the platted roadway, with its centroid inside the corridor - deeper than any of the four Lake Street records T-0196 looked at - and tools/generate_frontage_works.py refused two steps of Randolph's plank walk, 0.0 to 10.4 m along that face, naming this building in the refusal. THE REPAIR IS THIS RECORD'S OWN METHOD RUN AGAINST THIS PROJECT'S OWN LINE: the footprint is translated 4.981 m along the face's inward normal - dE -0.040 m, dN -4.981 m in local ENU, so UTM E 447538.25 N 4637126.21 becomes E 447538.21 N 4637121.23 - which leaves its north wall 1.50 m back from the committed frontage line. THE SQUARE IS NOT SUBDIVIDED, so there is no lot line to stand off: 1.50 m is plat_occupancy.LOT_MARGIN_M, the plat module's own margin off a boundary, and it is the same figure the reconciled South Water and Lake records took off their lot lines (T-0127, T-0198, T-0199). NOTHING ALONG THE STREET MOVED: the along-face position, the block, the corner and the side are untouched, and so is the confidence grade - re-deriving a coordinate from better geometry is not new evidence, and Andreas's 'northwest corner of the court-house square' is what it always was. WHAT THIS DOES NOT REPAIR: the 20 m working uncertainty stated above is unchanged and dwarfs this 4.98 m, so the move is a reconciliation between two of this project's own lines and not a claim to have located the jail better. The facade bearing stays 0 while this face runs at 0.46 degrees, which leaves the front wall between 1.50 and 1.55 m back across its width; that skew is not corrected here, because rotating a record is a second claim and this one is a repair. V4 ENCLOSURE/ACCESS RECONSTRUCTION 2026-10-30: the earlier exact northing was a chosen setback derived from the public-square street line, not an attested building coordinate. Andreas attests the northwest part of the square, not the exact setback. Move only 1.30 m south within the stated roughly20 m working uncertainty, retaining easting, bearing, core fabric, footprint, parcel and every committed street input. This finite R placement allows the existing1.80 m native doorway approach plus0.25 m to the continuous palisade axis atN-269.25 (0.16 m beyond a180 mm backing post), rather than preserving an invented centre gap that is absent from the1902 drawing. The exact1.30 m is an access/layout convention, not survey evidence or a measured pictorial distance. The1836-captioned plate does not establish the July1835 arrangement; continuity remains R. The earlier placement and plat-reconciliation history above is retained as history, not a claim that the later R setback is derived.
